```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Artic is the browser-based annotation tool. `annotate()` starts a
small local web server for a corpus and open Artic on it; saving in the browser
writes straight back to the corpus. These chunks are shown, not run, because
they start a server and open a browser.

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
library(reindeer)
corp <- demo_corpus()
```

## Edit a corpus

```{r annotate}
annotate(corp)                                       # everything
annotate(corp, session_pattern = "000.*")            # some sessions
annotate(corp, bundle_pattern = "msajc01.*")         # some bundles
```

Patterns are regular expressions. Change the address with `port =`, `host =`,
`auto_open_url = FALSE`, `browser =` or `use_viewer =`; `debug = TRUE` prints the
WebSocket traffic. Stop the server by closing the tab or with
`httpuv::stopAllServers()`.

## Review a query result

Pass a segment list to `annotate()` and Artic opens it as a
playlist with one time anchor per segment, stepping through them in the order
of the rows.

```{r review}
stops <- query(corp, "Phonetic == t")
annotate(stops)
```

Sort first to decide the order. Reviewing the least reliable measurements
first is a good use:

```{r sorted}
vowels <- query(corp, "Phonetic == V")
formants <- quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest)
annotate(formants |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(F1_Hz)))
```

When the segment list came from `quantify()`, the computed tracks are drawn
over the spectrogram as overlays, so you can see what the measurement did.
Choose them with `tracks =`, or turn them off with `tracks = character()`.

## Setup

reindeer ships with a build of Artic. To use another one, give its directory
for one call, for the session, or for all sessions:

```{r setup-artic}
annotate(corp, app_dir = "../artic/dist")
options(reindeer.artic.dir = "/path/to/artic/dist")
Sys.setenv(ARTIC_DIR = "/path/to/artic/dist")
```

Lookup order: the `app_dir` argument, the `reindeer.artic.dir` option, the
`ARTIC_DIR` environment variable, the bundled build, then a sibling
`../artic/dist`.

## Good to know

* Edits are saved to the `_annot.json` files; the query cache follows
  automatically the next time the corpus is opened or queried.
* The corpus's `_DBconfig.json` is never written by a session; view settings
  (which levels and tracks are shown) live only in memory.
* `annotate()` is also the name of a ggplot2 function. If the first argument is
  not a corpus or segment list, the call is passed on to ggplot2, so both work.
* The old `serve()` and `serve_app()` are stubs that point here.
